title: The merge tool waits for CI to finish, not for a fixed 30 minutes
why: Oct 22: the merge tool's 30-minute wait ran out while #562's last Windows job was still running; nothing was red, and the session had to start the wait again. The same day the macOS job cap was raised from 25 to 50 minutes because it kept cancelling the batch's macOS job, and one timing test in the report-gate tests failed once in a full run and passed alone.
note: Filed Oct 22 from the goal session's message. Cause found at 987f682: stamp.json waits 30 minutes, but a CI job may run 36 (50 after #562), so the wait was too short before #562 too. Brief written: set the wait from the job caps and add a check that keeps them in step. Advisor take, Oct 22: neither this nor c33 blocks work now, so keep the order; good as a small lane in the next batch. Your question, Oct 23: must CI be time-limited? Checked at 1842e56: skill ci-hygiene step 5 caps each job at about 2x its slowest green run; all 13 jobs carry caps, 3 to 50 minutes (GitHub's default is 360). Your word, Oct 23: keep the job caps (a hung job would hold the batch for 6 hours, and macOS minutes cost the most); the merge wait follows the longest cap plus 5, as this step's brief says. Oct 23: merged with c39 (CI caps go stale) into one goal-2 lane, ci-time-caps, batch 3 (full text on c37). Advisor answer to the goal session, Oct 23 (not the owner's word): the timing test has no record, so the lane runs all six wall-clock bounds in lint/test_gates.py, the whole file 20 times under load; the 70% warning adds startedAt and completedAt to the existing gh pr checks call and reads caps from the workflow files, no new call; the timeout verdict is a cancelled check that ran at least its cap, with no step data (run 39074284633's timed-out job shows every step as success). Raising the merge wait 30 to 55 is item 4 as approved.
ask:
# c34. The merge tool waits for CI to finish, not for a fixed 30 minutes

Checked claude-settings main at 987f682 and batch branch batch-oct22c (#562).

Cause: .github/stamp.json sets merge.deadlineMinutes to 30 (merge/merge.py MERGE_DEFAULTS is 45).
The CI jobs' own caps in .github/workflows/gates.yml are longer: one job has timeout-minutes 36
on main, and #562 raises the macOS job to 50. So a green but slow run outlasts the wait, as on
#562 on Oct 22. actions/stamp/README.md already says to set deadlineMinutes "to a bit more than
your slowest required check"; nothing checks that it is.

Brief, claude-settings (after #562 merges, or as a lane in the next batch):
1. Set merge.deadlineMinutes in .github/stamp.json to the largest timeout-minutes of a job in
   .github/workflows plus 5 (55 once #562 is on main).
2. Add one check, in the home that already validates stamp.json (find it; extend it, do not add a
   second): it fails when deadlineMinutes is below the largest job timeout-minutes in the
   workflows. Test: red on main (30 below 36), green after step 1.
3. The report-gate timing test that failed once in a full run and passed alone: run it 20 times on
   main. If it fails, fix the cause (the time it reads, or what it races), never add a retry or
   a longer sleep. If it never fails, say so and change nothing.
Report: the files changed, the test red then green, and the 20-run count.
